objective: Build a repeatable experiment that compares solo Codex, solo Claude, Codex-to-Claude critique, and Claude-to-Codex critique workflows using governed TORC handoffs and deterministic task evidence.
success_evidence: Every workflow uses a pinned task fixture, harness version, model, effort, tool policy, assignment, and output contract.
Cross-provider targets receive a model-visible claim capsule while full provenance and authority metadata remain in a hash-bound control envelope.
Codex and Claude usage is normalized into input, cached-input, cache-write, reasoning-output, and output token fields when the harness supplies them.
Wall-clock stages, failed attempts, operator interventions, test results, and claim-resolution failures are preserved.
No comparative claim is made until independent fixtures and repeat runs complete.
non_goals: A universal ranking of Codex and Claude.
Provider routing, credential custody, or model inference inside TORC core.
Automatic production delegation or edits outside isolated experiment worktrees.
Treating model votes as stronger evidence than tests, policy checks, or provenance.
Parsing or recreating provider-native opaque compaction artifacts.
stop_conditions: The harness cannot isolate the fixture oracle or hidden tests.
A workflow cannot report effective model and effort controls.
The foreign critic does not improve deterministic task quality over native review.
The claim capsule loses a required constraint or cannot resolve every cited claim.
Live usage cannot be attributed to a frozen workflow attempt.
